Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. Standalone result-only packages expose the same results without checked-input metadata. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains an ordinary empty record, and Option presence, arrays, and the active or inactive Mark branches remain distinct. Full packages validate nullary checked constructors and exact rejection and recovery. Result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as ordinary GMP integers in C and cpp_int values in C++. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. The generated C/GMP, C++ multiprecision, C# BigInteger, Java BigInteger and Kotlin BigInteger records expose only proof-free payloads. Full packages validate all eight indexed inputs through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserve rejected caller values, recover on the next valid call and return all eight proof-free results. Standalone result-only packages expose the same results without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a nominal empty carrier; C uses one non-semantic uint8_t storage byte solely to give the structure a legal nonzero size, while C++ uses an empty structure. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains an ordinary empty record, and Option presence, arrays, and the active or inactive Mark branches remain distinct. Full packages validate nullary checked constructors and exact rejection and recovery. Result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures."

edits.current: "scope": "First installed slice: Interval, Sized 3 and Bounded 0 101 at top-level parameters/results, including multiple checked inputs, normalizing constructors and result-only output. Additional nested C/C++ acceptance: Two independent author roots reproduce complete C and C++ packages before source-free offline installation. Independent C11/GMP and C++20 callers replay unchanged after physical relocation, giving four replay executions plus two setup executions per selection. The full API checks direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, both Except branches, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, including exact per-site constructors, normalization, complete rejected-input snapshots and recovery. Independent controls reject every missing record and coordinated report, resource, model and package mutation. Nested checked-record C/C++ acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete packages from two roots. Independent C11/GMP and C++20 callers install offline after author removal and replay after physical relocation on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor. Constructor/source entry counts and peak memory are unmeasured. These local runs do not establish hosted or glibc 2.38 release-floor acceptance. Additional inherited native acceptance: The native installed lane authenticates the ordinary full inherited checked-record package selection for c, cpp. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. Hosted GitHub Linux x64 acceptance with an explicit glibc 2.38 package floor and load ceiling 12. Four ordinary/reviewed full/result-only selections reproduce complete C and C++ packages from two author roots, install offline after author removal, and replay unchanged independent C11/GMP and C++20 callers after physical relocation. Parent and child constructors, repeated positions with different constructor selections, nested inheritance, aliases and invalid inner and outer values are exercised; result-only packages erase input-constructor metadata. Complete original C and C++ archives, receipts, caller sources, execution records, the original TAP, the hosted verification and the exact producer source closure are retained. External compiler and operating-system distributions are not retained. Other hosts, callbacks and owned positions require separate evidence. This archive does not itself promote support. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Additional recursive native acceptance: The native installed lane authenticates the ordinary mutual recursive checked-record selection for c, cpp. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. Hosted Ubuntu 24.04 Linux x64 acceptance records the observed glibc runtime and enforces a glibc 2.38 package floor; other operating systems and architectures remain separate requirements. Ordinary source and independently reviewed Binding IR routes reproduce complete C and C++ packages from two isolated author roots, remove author sources, install offline, relocate and replay without consumer sources or compilers. The immutable C and C++ callers cover mutual records and variants, aliases, arrays and options, active branches, exact Fin and Subtype diagnostics, malformed values, cycles, depth limits, preserved rejected inputs and recovery. Proof fields are erased, recursive nominal identities stay distinct, and results contain no runtime proof constructors. Callbacks, owned values, asynchronous calls, retained identity, dependent index kinds, open dependent records and zero-payload records remain separate requirements. Original package archives, receipts, models, source inputs, caller sources, reports, controls, TAP, checker output, toolchain log and exact producer, checker and archiver source closures are retained; external compiler and operating-system distributions remain trusted. edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as ordinary GMP integers in C and cpp_int values in C++. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. The generated C/GMP, C++ multiprecision, C# BigInteger, Java BigInteger and Kotlin BigInteger records expose only proof-free payloads. Full packages validate all eight indexed inputs through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserve rejected caller values, recover on the next valid call and return all eight proof-free results. Standalone result-only packages expose the same results without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a nominal empty carrier; C uses one non-semantic uint8_t storage byte solely to give the structure a legal nonzero size, while C++ uses an empty structure. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains an ordinary empty record, and Option presence, arrays, and the active or inactive Mark branches remain distinct. Full packages validate nullary checked constructors and exact rejection and recovery. Result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures."

edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. Generic records, other indices and dynamic dependent payloads are not covered. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. Generic records, other indices and dynamic dependent payloads are not covered. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices stay in authenticated type metadata and are not host fields. JavaScript and TypeScript pass proof-free objects: On, Off, EmptyToken, UnicodeToken, ZeroToken and WideToken expose count: bigint; Ab exposes size: bigint; EmptySized exposes data: bigint[]. The full package checks records indexed by both booleans, \"ab\", the empty string, \"λ🌱\", zero and 340282366920938463463374607431768211457 through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserves rejected caller values and recovers on the next valid call. Standalone result-only packages return the same proof-free objects without input-constructor metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an owned JavaScript object with no payload properties and as Readonly<Record<PropertyKey, never>> in TypeScript. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains distinct, Option presence, array length and active or inactive Mark branches remain explicit. Full packages validate the nullary checked constructor and exact rejection and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures."

edits.current: "scope": "First installed slice: Interval, Sized 3 and Bounded 0 101 at top-level parameters/results, including multiple checked inputs, normalizing constructors and result-only output. Additional installed browser-package acceptance: Two reproduced author builds, source-free offline installation, strict TypeScript and two Node executions including physical installed-tree relocation. Twelve Chromium/Firefox/WebKit page, React production/Strict Mode and worker executions cover 51 lifecycle observations. Full packages check 16176 assertions, 3031 expected rejections, 8088 calls/snapshots and 3031 recoveries per observation, including constructor selection and normalization. Additional nested checked-record acceptance: Two independent author builds reproduce complete component and runtime archives before source-free offline npm installation. Installed JavaScript and strict TypeScript callers replay after physical relocation. Chromium, Firefox and WebKit each execute page, React production/Strict Mode and dedicated-worker consumers, including missing-Wasm recovery, for twelve browser executions and fifty-one lifecycle observations. The full package checks direct and repeated parameters plus Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing record and active variant fields; exact failures preserve caller graphs and later calls recover. Producer, browser-consumer and destructive-checker revisions are independently frozen. Nested checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copy positions. Generic records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Other host targets require their own installed evidence. These local Linux x64 Node, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit runs do not establish hosted acceptance. Constructor dispatch counts and peak memory are unmeasured. Complete npm component/runtime archives and original report inputs are retained; browser binaries, React framework archives and generated deployments are represented by recorded identities and observations rather than copied. Additional inherited browser acceptance: The browser installed lane authenticates the ordinary full inherited checked-record package selection for node-javascript, node-typescript, browser-javascript, browser-react, browser-worker. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, child checked fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections and constructor-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only npm packages. Node JavaScript, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit execute source-free installed packages; browser contexts cover plain pages, React production and StrictMode, and dedicated workers. Complete component/runtime npm archives, installed receipts, reports, controls, TAP streams and browser observations are retained. Browser binaries and generated deployment directories are represented by their recorded identities and observations. The evidence applies to the exact Linux x64 Node and browser versions recorded in this index. Other hosts require independent installed acceptance. The hosted workflow serializes the four route/mode selections and caps Lean, compiler and build parallelism; peak memory and constructor-dispatch counts are not measured. This archive establishes installed npm/browser behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Additional recursive browser acceptance: The browser installed lane authenticates the ordinary mutual recursive checked-record selection for node-javascript, node-typescript, browser-javascript, browser-react, browser-worker. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The archive authenticates local Linux x64 Node, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit execution; it does not claim hosted-runner acceptance. Acceptance covers the tested finite mutually recursive Envelope and Branch records/variants, transparent aliases, Array and Option copies; host cycles are rejected and traversal is bounded. Callback, owned, asynchronous and retained-identity positions remain separate requirements. Browser binaries, framework archives and generated deployments are represented by recorded identities and observations rather than copied. Constructor dispatch counts and peak memory remain unmeasured. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions. Results contain copied payload fields with proofs erased. Both ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Rust Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as num_bigint::BigUint values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Rust adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, tuple, Result, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than Rust record fields. Generated structs use BigUint for Nat payloads such as `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element. Full crates exercise exact per-site constructors, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only crates expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a nominal empty Rust struct with no application payload. Token keeps its generated Unit field, plain empty Marker remains a distinct nominal struct, Option presence stays explicit, vectors retain length and independent elements, and active or inactive Mark branches remain distinct. Full crates validate nullary checked constructors and exact rejection and recovery. Result-only crates project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures."

Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. The tested Component Model Packet is a WIT record whose Fin 10 digit and checked Nat Subtype word are canonical list<u32> limbs. A Holder record nests Packet, and the packet case of Choice carries it in its active branch. Generated WIT adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller value tree and output sentinel, and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free WIT records without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than WIT record fields. Generated records expose Nat payloads such as `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element as exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs. Full components exercise exact per-site constructors, malformed-Nat host refusal, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only components expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness follows the generator's WIT empty-carrier convention as enum witness { empty }; this is a representation choice, not a Lean semantic distinction. Token remains record token { tag: unit }, Marker uses its own empty enum, option presence, list length and Mark branches remain explicit. Full component packages validate the nullary checked constructor and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures."

edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass generated record objects containing Math::BigInt values and plain array references, without proofs. Lean runs the selected constructor for each input; it may normalize accepted data, or reject with the parameter and constructor name while preserving caller values. Results contain independent copied payload fields with proofs erased. Ordinary and reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as Math::BigInt values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Perl adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than Perl fields. Generated blessed records use `Math::BigInt` for `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element. Full packages exercise exact per-site constructors, negative-Nat host refusal, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only packages expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an exact blessed Perl class backed by a plain empty hash. Token retains its Unit value, Marker remains a distinct blessed class, undef stays distinct from a present Witness, arrays retain length, and Mark keeps its branch. Full CPAN packages validate exact classes across four ABI interpreters, the nullary constructor and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures."

Author and build roots are removed before offline installation and physical relocation; unchanged weak and strict callers run in eight Node embedded/Composer and four Chromium bundled startup/lazy contexts, giving twelve executions per selection. The full API checks direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, both Except branches, Holder.packet and the active ChoicePacket.value field, including exact per-site constructors, normalization, complete rejected-input snapshots and recovery. Checked-record PHP-Wasm acceptance covers the established top-level Interval, Sized 3 and Bounded 0 101 forms plus the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic checked records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete Composer API, npm component and npm shared-runtime archives from two author roots, remove author and build roots, install offline, physically relocate each installation, and run unchanged weak and strict callers in eight Node and four Chromium contexts. The runs use wasm32 PHP 8.4.1, Node 22.23.2 and Chromium 152.0.7977.75 on Linux x64 with 32-bit machine words and a recorded 20.0 host-load admission ceiling. The archive retains complete packages, receipts, deployment callers, execution records and both producer and verifier source closures. Consumer PHP source remains required at runtime. The prepared PHP-Wasm runtime and browser remain trusted inputs; hosted acceptance remains assigned to the dedicated workflow. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured. Additional inherited php-wasm acceptance: The php-wasm installed lane authenticates the reviewed full inherited checked-record package selection for php-wasm. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, checked child fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections, and proof-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only prepared package sets. Each package set contains the Composer API, npm component, and shared npm runtime archives reproduced from two author roots. Offline consumers execute after source and handoff removal, before and after relocation, in twelve Node and Chromium loading contexts. Complete archives, receipts, callers, execution records, TAP, and producer, checker, and archiver source closures are retained. Consumer PHP source remains required when the installed package executes. Compiler, operating-system, browser, Node, PHP, Composer, and npm distributions remain trusted inputs. This archive establishes installed PHP-Wasm behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Additional recursive php-wasm acceptance: The php-wasm installed lane authenticates the reviewed recursive recursive checked-record selection for php-wasm. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The fixtures cover the self-recursive Packet graph and the mutually recursive Envelope/Step graph with Option and Array carriers. Checked fields are limited to Fin 3 and the tested plusOne/plusTwo Nat Subtype constructors. The PHP-Wasm caller reuses the native-PHP caller and oracle byte for byte; acceptance does not follow from native PHP and every cell runs inside wasm32 PHP-Wasm. Generic, inherited, open dependent and zero-payload records, callbacks and explicitly owned positions remain separate work. Consumer PHP source remains required when the installed package executes. These local Linux x64 runs do not establish hosted release-floor acceptance. Compiler, operating-system, browser, Node, PHP, Composer and npm distributions remain trusted. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions. The php-wasm installed lane authenticates the reviewed mutual recursive checked-record selection for php-wasm. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The fixtures cover the self-recursive Packet graph and the mutually recursive Envelope/Step graph with Option and Array carriers. Checked fields are limited to Fin 3 and the tested plusOne/plusTwo Nat Subtype constructors. The PHP-Wasm caller reuses the native-PHP caller and oracle byte for byte; acceptance does not follow from native PHP and every cell runs inside wasm32 PHP-Wasm. Generic, inherited, open dependent and zero-payload records, callbacks and explicitly owned positions remain separate work. Consumer PHP source remains required when the installed package executes. These local Linux x64 runs do not establish hosted release-floor acceptance. Compiler, operating-system, browser, Node, PHP, Composer and npm distributions remain trusted. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions. Additional hosted closed-index acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39370772629 rebuilt this full reviewed-ir PHP-Wasm selection on Ubuntu 24.04. Two author roots reproduce the complete Composer API, npm component and shared-runtime archives, remove author and build roots, install offline, relocate the installation and replay unchanged weak and strict callers in Node and Chromium. The full API exercises all eight checked inputs, exact constructor refusals, unchanged rejected values, recovery and all eight proof-free indexed results. The archive authenticates the original workflow, job, artifact, compiler probes, runtime logs, TAP, reports, receipts, executions and exact source identities. Hosted PHP-Wasm value-index acceptance covers only the archived top-level copied checked-record parameter and result sites with closed Bool, String and Nat indices. Full packages cover parameters and results; standalone result-only packages cover results only. Open or opaque indices; Int, Char, fixed-width and platform-width integers, Fin, functions, proofs, instances and other index kinds; checked-record fields, callbacks and owned positions; value-carrying dependent payloads; and zero-payload checked records remain unreviewed here. The run covers weak and strict callers, embedded and Composer arrangements, startup and lazy loading in Node and Chromium on wasm32 PHP 8.4.1. Complete Composer, component and shared-runtime archives, receipts, reports, deployments, execution records, original workflow records and source closures are retained; external Lean, Nix, PHP-Wasm, Emscripten, Node, Chromium and operating-system toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs. Other host targets require separate installed evidence. Additional hosted zero-payload PHP-Wasm acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39621064577 rebuilt the reviewed-ir PHP-Wasm selection on Ubuntu 24.04. Two independent author roots reproduced the complete prepared package before author removal, source-free offline installation and unchanged replay after physical relocation. The package runs the selected nullary Witness constructor at every checked input, keeps rejected values unchanged, recovers on the next valid call and projects proof-erased results. The retained archive authenticates every original artifact byte, route result, caller observation and exact producer, consumer, checker and archiver source closure. Hosted zero-payload PHP-Wasm acceptance covers only the retained Witness, Token, Marker, Option, Array and Mark fixtures at copied parameter and result sites in four ordinary/reviewed full/result-only packages. It does not promote checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, other zero-payload shapes or another host. External Lean, consumer-language, package-manager and operating-system toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs. Additional owned checked-record acceptance: Fresh Lean ordinary-source and independently reviewed packages exercise the copied Window check inside Booking and the owned Claim check across Ticket resources. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, exact constructor rejection before transfer, synchronous host callbacks, invalid explicit recovery before callback entry, returned Lean closures, exception identity and cleanup. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced proof-free Claim results without checked inputs, transfer or callback metadata. Every route reproduces Composer API, npm component and npm shared-runtime archives, removes author/build roots, installs offline, physically relocates the installed tree and passes eight Node plus eight Chromium startup/lazy weak/strict executions with zero live identities and later-request recovery. Additional hosted dependent acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39857552688, job 120100093905, artifact 12464147584 rebuilt the full reviewed-ir php-wasm package selection. The author routes reproduce the package, remove author sources, install without network access and replay unchanged typed callers. The full API exercises valid and rejected dependent inputs through the selected constructor, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results. The retained archive authenticates every original artifact byte, route result, package, caller observation and selected source. Hosted dependent checked-record acceptance covers only the retained top-level copied DependentRecords.Dependent parameter and result sites, whose Fin bound field depends on the runtime bound field and whose proof is rebuilt by the selected mkDependent constructor. Full packages cover parameters and results; standalone result-only packages cover results only. Dependent fields of other kinds, nested or recursive dependent records, checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, open or opaque indices and zero-payload records remain unreviewed here. The PHP-Wasm cells are the shared result tracked by #1461 and are not inferred from native PHP. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures."

The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, child checked fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections, and constructor-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only Cargo packages. Complete crates are reproduced from two author roots, installed offline, executed before and after relocation, and reduced to one source-free executable. Complete crate and dependency archives, receipts, inventories, caller binaries, execution records, TAP, controls, and producer/checker/archive source closures are retained. The package floor is glibc 2.38; the archive records and verifies the hosted runner's independently observed glibc version. Compiler, operating-system, Rust, Cargo, linker, and glibc distributions remain trusted inputs. This archive establishes installed Rust behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Additional recursive rust acceptance: The rust installed lane authenticates the ordinary recursive recursive checked-record selection for rust. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The fixtures cover the tested self-recursive Packet graph and mutually recursive Envelope/Step graph; runtime values are finite and bounded. Checked fields are limited to Fin 3 and the tested Nat Subtype constructors. Acceptance covers the exact identities, aliases, active branches, traversal limits, diagnostics, recovery paths and positions exercised by the immutable Rust caller. Generic, inherited, open dependent and zero-payload records remain separate work. Callbacks, resources and explicitly owned or borrowed positions remain separate work. These local Linux x64/glibc 2.36 runs do not establish hosted release-floor acceptance. The original four selections were individually authenticated after serial execution; their separate TAP streams do not encode cross-selection timestamps. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured; Rust, Cargo, the system linker and glibc remain trusted toolchain inputs. edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass the generated record's runtime payload fields, without proof values. The selected Lean constructor checks each input and may normalize it; rejection identifies the parameter and constructor and preserves caller data. Results contain copied payload fields with proofs erased. Both ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Rust Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as num_bigint::BigUint values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Rust adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, tuple, Result, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures."

## Owned checked records

[Hosted owned checked-record acceptance](../evidence/owned-checked-record-promotion-20261024.md) covers C on ordinary Lean-source and independently reviewed package routes. The tested forms are `Booking`, whose `Window` field is copied and checked, and `Claim`, whose `Ticket` resource stays owned while its quota is checked. Proof fields do not cross the boundary.

Use the generated record carriers and keep the `Ticket` owner alive for the call. A borrowed call leaves the caller's owner intact. A transferred call validates the record before moving that owner; rejected inputs remain usable. Leased results require the cleanup described by this language's ownership API. Synchronous callbacks exchange proof-free `Claim` values: host-produced replies and inputs to a returned Lean closure are checked, while Lean-produced arguments and results are projected without proof fields.

Full packages exercise inputs, results, the nested `Window` field, synchronous callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced `Claim` results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. A successful result-only package is not evidence for those input or callback paths.

This acceptance does not cover `Grant` and its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. Earlier copied, generic and dependent-record receipts retain their own narrower scopes.

The tested forms are `Booking`, whose `Window` field is copied and checked, and `Claim`, whose `Ticket` resource stays owned while its quota is checked. Proof fields do not cross the boundary.

Use the generated record carriers and keep the `Ticket` owner alive for the call. A borrowed call leaves the caller's owner intact. A transferred call validates the record before moving that owner; rejected inputs remain usable. Leased results require the cleanup described by this language's ownership API. Synchronous callbacks exchange proof-free `Claim` values: host-produced replies and inputs to a returned Lean closure are checked, while Lean-produced arguments and results are projected without proof fields.

Full packages exercise inputs, results, the nested `Window` field, synchronous callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced `Claim` results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. A successful result-only package is not evidence for those input or callback paths.

This acceptance does not cover `Grant` and its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. Earlier copied, generic and dependent-record receipts retain their own narrower scopes.

## Owned checked records

[Hosted owned checked-record acceptance](../evidence/owned-checked-record-promotion-20261024.md) covers Python on ordinary Lean-source and independently reviewed package routes. The tested forms are `Booking`, whose `Window` field is copied and checked, and `Claim`, whose `Ticket` resource stays owned while its quota is checked. Proof fields do not cross the boundary.

Use the generated record carriers and keep the `Ticket` owner alive for the call. A borrowed call leaves the caller's owner intact. A transferred call validates the record before moving that owner; rejected inputs remain usable. Leased results require the cleanup described by this language's ownership API. Synchronous callbacks exchange proof-free `Claim` values: host-produced replies and inputs to a returned Lean closure are checked, while Lean-produced arguments and results are projected without proof fields.

Full packages exercise inputs, results, the nested `Window` field, synchronous callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced `Claim` results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. A successful result-only package is not evidence for those input or callback paths.

This acceptance does not cover `Grant` and its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. Earlier copied, generic and dependent-record receipts retain their own narrower scopes.

## Owned checked records

[Hosted owned checked-record acceptance](../evidence/owned-checked-record-promotion-20261024.md) covers Rust on ordinary Lean-source and independently reviewed package routes. The tested forms are `Booking`, whose `Window` field is copied and checked, and `Claim`, whose `Ticket` resource stays owned while its quota is checked. Proof fields do not cross the boundary.

Use the generated record carriers and keep the `Ticket` owner alive for the call. A borrowed call leaves the caller's owner intact. A transferred call validates the record before moving that owner; rejected inputs remain usable. Leased results require the cleanup described by this language's ownership API. Synchronous callbacks exchange proof-free `Claim` values: host-produced replies and inputs to a returned Lean closure are checked, while Lean-produced arguments and results are projected without proof fields.

Full packages exercise inputs, results, the nested `Window` field, synchronous callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced `Claim` results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. A successful result-only package is not evidence for those input or callback paths.

This acceptance does not cover `Grant` and its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. Earlier copied, generic and dependent-record receipts retain their own narrower scopes.

## Owned checked records

[Hosted owned checked-record acceptance](evidence/owned-checked-record-promotion-20261024.md) covers Node JavaScript, TypeScript, browser pages, React and dedicated workers on ordinary Lean-source and independently reviewed package routes. The tested forms are `Booking`, whose `Window` field is copied and checked, and `Claim`, whose `Ticket` resource stays owned while its quota is checked. Proof fields do not cross the boundary.

Use the generated record carriers and keep the `Ticket` owner alive for the call. A borrowed call leaves the caller's owner intact. A transferred call validates the record before moving that owner; rejected inputs remain usable. Leased results require the cleanup described by this language's ownership API. Synchronous callbacks exchange proof-free `Claim` values: host-produced replies and inputs to a returned Lean closure are checked, while Lean-produced arguments and results are projected without proof fields.

Full packages exercise inputs, results, the nested `Window` field, synchronous callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced `Claim` results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. A successful result-only package is not evidence for those input or callback paths.

This acceptance does not cover `Grant` and its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. Earlier copied, generic and dependent-record receipts retain their own narrower scopes.

## Owned checked records

[Hosted owned checked-record acceptance](evidence/owned-checked-record-promotion-20261024.md) covers native PHP and PHP-Wasm, each backed by an independent hosted archive on ordinary Lean-source and independently reviewed package routes. The tested forms are `Booking`, whose `Window` field is copied and checked, and `Claim`, whose `Ticket` resource stays owned while its quota is checked. Proof fields do not cross the boundary.

Use the generated record carriers and keep the `Ticket` owner alive for the call. A borrowed call leaves the caller's owner intact. A transferred call validates the record before moving that owner; rejected inputs remain usable. Leased results require the cleanup described by this language's ownership API. Synchronous callbacks exchange proof-free `Claim` values: host-produced replies and inputs to a returned Lean closure are checked, while Lean-produced arguments and results are projected without proof fields.

Full packages exercise inputs, results, the nested `Window` field, synchronous callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced `Claim` results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata.
